text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes treatment involves lifestyle adjustments, blood sugar monitoring, oral or injectable medications, and sometimes weight-loss surgery or insulin therapy.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle adjustments, blood sugar monitoring, oral or injectable medications, and sometimes weight-loss surgery or insulin therapy

list.snippet: Diet Changes: Focus on whole foods, lean proteins, non-starchy vegetables, and complex carbohydrates while limiting refined sugars and processed foods.
Physical Activity: Regular exercise (such as brisk walking or aerobic activity) helps improve insulin sensitivity and manage weight.
Weight Management: Losing a modest amount of body weight can significantly improve blood sugar regulation.
Metformin: Typically the first-line oral medication prescribed; it reduces glucose production in the liver and improves insulin sensitivity.
Sulfonylureas & Glinides: Stimulate the pancreas to produce and release more insulin (e.g., glipizide, glimepiride).
DPP-4 Inhibitors: Help lower blood sugar by prolonging the activity of natural gut hormones that stimulate insulin.
SGLT2 Inhibitors: Help the kidneys remove excess glucose from the body through urine.
Thiazolidinediones (TZDs): Improve insulin sensitivity in muscle and fat tissue.
GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Injectable medications that stimulate meal-dependent insulin release, slow digestion, and often support weight loss.
Insulin Therapy: Long-acting, short-acting, or premixed insulins may be added if oral options and lifestyle changes no longer keep blood sugar in the target range.
Blood Sugar Tracking: Using a blood glucose meter or a continuous glucose monitor (CGM) to track levels daily or in real time.
Weight-Loss (Bariatric) Surgery: Considered for adults with a high body mass index (BMI) or severe insulin resistance to help manage or potentially drive diabetes into remission.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about medication classes and management strategies through the American Diabetes Association or the Mayo Clinic Guide to Type 2 Diabetes.
